notes: Handwritten continuation and closing of a letter signed P. Deligne. It describes local extensions, transition isomorphisms, the written cocycle condition and an obstruction arrow, then says the construction also works analytically and invokes GAGA. The first remark mentions algebraic spaces, rigid analytic spaces and formal schemes. A second underlined heading is cancelled, while its colon remains live; no text follows that colon. No title, date, salutation or manuscript page number appears on this sheet. The only page-like numeral is archive 75 at lower left, kept solely as a comment. No explicit author question mark or stated doubt occurs. H provides description only and is unavailable for collation: every h_reading is null and diff_h is false. The whole image was viewed once for layout, followed by half a then half b once each. Half b begins at whole-image y=920. Nine retained crops were each delivered and visually inspected once in batches of three; requested and actual views are recorded in crop_manifest_c76.json. No OCR, external source, other page, peer reading or TeX engine was used.
math_reading_decisions: The unmarked C-context cover and restriction targets are confirmed: U_i, X_0, inserted U\prime_i, and \mathscr{N}\mid U_i. Primes are short raised strokes; i is a short low suffix; restriction bars are tall single vertical strokes.

The first H has one ordinary upright-and-crossbar structure, followed by a raised 0 and a still higher parenthesized alg. The first display is H^{0^{(\mathrm{alg})}}, with actual parentheses around alg.

The sheaf-functor initials have looped/curling forms, transcribed \mathscr{E}xt^1 and \mathscr{H}om. The cohomology H and each K are ordinary single-stroke capitals. The ideal letter is looped \mathscr{N}. Each occurrence was checked on this page.

The transition arrow has one shaft, a right arrowhead, and a single wavy stroke above. Both restrictions show U_i\cap U_j with an arched intersection sign. The source suffix resolves to j; the target remains i|j|k from its own merged strokes.

The recurring transition glyph is marked \unsure{\eta|n} at its first appearance and written \eta thereafter. The first symbol and all later copies have two stems, one descending farther; gamma is excluded from the alternatives. Lowered ij, jk and ik are independently read in the cocycle line.

The inline expression after par is d_2\eta as written, although the opening element is named e. The glyph after d_2 has the same descending two-stem shape as the transition symbols, not the small loop of the opening e. It has not been corrected to d_2e.

The last display has low numeral 2 after d, H^0 at the source, \mathscr{E}xt^1 inside it, and H^2 at the target with \mathscr{H}om. The long arrow points right and both outer expressions close with two parentheses.
